edge.title: The parcel you never sent
edge.setup: A call or SMS: a courier in your name is held — contraband, expired documents, a customs duty unpaid. There's a small fee to release it, or a case will be filed. Sometimes the caller knows your address, because it leaked from a delivery app.
edge.tell: An unexpected problem whose solution is a small immediate payment to a stranger.
move: No courier or customs process is ever resolved by phone to a UPI ID. Hang up.
If you genuinely expect a parcel, check the tracking number on the courier's own website — never via a link sent to you.
Report at cybercrime.gov.in; don't engage to 'find out more'.
edge.why: Small-fee scams work on expected value: ₹1,500 is below your threshold for serious scrutiny but above zero, and sent at scale. Noticing the shape — unexpected problem, immediate small payment, stranger's account — immunises you against the whole family at once.
edge.variants: Same shape: fake traffic-challan links, electricity bill disconnection SMS, 'your KYC will lapse' payments.

lens.name: Induced demand
lens.one_line: Adding road capacity creates new trips that fill it, so congestion returns at a higher throughput.
lens.detail: People who had given up on a route — shifted their timing, taken transit, moved closer — return once it gets easier. The new lane doesn't serve the old traffic; it reveals suppressed demand that was always there. Measured honestly, travel time often lands back where it started within a few years, now with more vehicles.
elsewhere: Build more parking and more people drive in.
Add engineers to a late project and the scope expands to absorb them.
Widen a hospital's OPD and the waiting room refills.
lens.test: When someone promises more capacity will fix congestion, ask: what was suppressed, and what happens when it comes back?
lens.today: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has received over 1,500 objections to tree felling for the Hebbal Short Tunnel, and DULT is drafting a new mobility plan amid Rs 1-lakh crore of mega projects (The Hindu, Deccan Herald). Each project is sold as relief for a corridor, but capacity added to a congested road tends to pull back the trips people had avoided. Judge a tunnel or flyover by what it does to your commute five years on, not its opening-day time saving.

moved.what: Liquor sales curbs apply from 21 October for Dasara processions and MLC polls (Times of India).
moved.so_what: Buy anything you need before the 21st, and plan for procession diversions and slow roads on the day.

moved.what: Tomato prices have crashed by up to 80% in Bengaluru, but the drop is not city-wide (Times of India).
moved.so_what: Check your own market's rate before stocking up; the 80% is the best case, not your vendor's price.

moved.what: The Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper is to be flagged off on 1 November (Deccan Herald), with a 16-hour journey (Times of India).
moved.so_what: If you need Mumbai around that week, watch IRCTC for fares and booking windows before they fill.

moved.what: A Bengaluru advocate was shot dead in a row over unpaid rent, after tenants returned saying they had the rent money (Times of India, NDTV).
moved.so_what: If you are a landlord with overdue rent, put the demand in writing and involve a third party instead of meeting the tenant alone.

moved.what: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has received over 1,500 objections to tree felling for the Hebbal Short Tunnel (The Hindu).
moved.so_what: If the Hebbal corridor is on your route, expect works and a contested timeline; do not plan around an opening date yet.

carry_over.prompt: A new buyer wants a large lot delivered first and promises to pay later: what is the tell?
carry_over.answer: A new buyer who wants the goods first and the money later is asking you to be their lender.
